questions.q: What is the first part of Mara's five-part briefing structure to Howard Okonjo?
options: The forward-looking recommendation
The discrepancy stated plainly: 14 reported by the audit vs. 19 reported by the automation, same access, same day
An apology on behalf of the compliance team
The new risk-register row, R-06
questions.explain: Mara opens with the discrepancy itself, stated plainly, before explaining why it happened -- giving Howard the headline fact before the explanation.

questions.q: How does Mara explain the root cause to Howard, consistent with Lesson 15's conclusion?
options: The audit team made a careless counting error

Both numbers were accurate for what each method measured -- the audit checked group membership only, the automation checked group membership and direct assignment, and the 5-account gap traced to unrevoked break-glass grants from the Substation 12 outage
The automation had a bug that inflated the count
Howard Okonjo authorized the wrong scope for the audit
questions.explain: Mara frames the root cause as a methodology gap, not an error by either tool or team -- exactly the distinction established in Lesson 15.

questions.q: Why does Mara deliberately avoid framing this as the compliance audit team's mistake when briefing Howard?
options: Because blaming the audit team is technically accurate but politically risky

Because the audit team followed its documented checklist correctly -- the checklist itself never included a step for direct assignment -- so framing it as their error would be inaccurate and would make them defensive instead of getting their buy-in on the real fix
Because Howard Okonjo personally wrote the audit checklist
Because the audit team no longer works at Hartwell
questions.explain: Mara uses the no-blame, process-cause framing from Lesson 15: the team executed its method correctly, so the fix is to the method's scope, not to the people -- and this framing also makes the compliance team more likely to support the recommended charter change.

questions.q: What is Mara's one recommendation that goes beyond the fix already made to the 5 accounts?
options: Replacing the compliance team with automated tooling entirely

Formally updating the compliance audit charter, for every Critical-tier segment, to require a direct-assignment check as a standard step -- not something that depends on Mara's automation happening to be running
Running the audit twice as often with the same method
Removing the OT/SCADA segment from audit scope entirely
questions.explain: Mara's closing recommendation targets the audit charter itself, so the category of gap doesn't recur on any Critical-tier segment -- a stronger outcome than fixing just this one instance.

questions.q: What does this briefing hand off directly to Lesson 19?
options: A request to re-open the Substation 12 incident ticket
The full resolved discrepancy -- root cause, validated fix, and new risk-register entry with its compensating control -- formalized next into Hartwell's after-action report
A decision to cancel the zero-trust segmentation pilot
A new board-level mandate unrelated to this finding
questions.explain: Lesson 19 picks up this exact material -- the discrepancy, root cause, fix, and R-06 -- and formalizes it into Hartwell's after-action report.
